blocking_issues.observed: Both editions state that September 2026 Korea merchandise trade surplus was approximately USD 49.97bn and that October's USD 42.50bn surplus declined by USD 7.47bn.
blocking_issues.verified_evidence: Korea MOTIR's original 1 October 2026 September trade release reports exports USD 120.94bn, imports USD 71.09bn, and surplus USD 49.85bn (498.5 eok USD). The October 1 November release reports surplus USD 42.50bn. Using these primary-source vintages, September-to-October change is -USD 7.35bn, not -USD 7.47bn. Reuters reports USD 49.97bn in some coverage, but the report cites only October MOTIR release [1] for this comparison and does not disclose an alternative revised vintage.
blocking_issues.required_fix: Reconcile and explicitly name the chosen September data vintage; under MOTIR's original September release use USD 49.85bn and -USD 7.35bn, with a direct dated September source reference in both locales. If a revised official September figure is used instead, provide the revised primary document and label its vintage; recheck all arithmetic and related prose.

blocking_issues.observed: Both editions describe September 2026 Korean merchandise-export year-on-year growth as approximately +83.7%, compared with October +93.7%.

The article's +83.7% is inconsistent with that official source and the article lacks a September original-source bibliography entry.
blocking_issues.required_fix: Change the September growth figure to +83.5% in both languages, or substantiate a later official revision with its observation vintage and primary URL; add the September primary-source reference to both end bibliographies.

contrary_evidence: MOTIR October release confirms 93.7% y/y export growth and 259.4% semiconductor growth, with +34% non-chip export value and October export total below September; the central analysis need not be rewritten wholesale.
China October manufacturing PMI 49.3 and new export orders 48.7 are diffusion indices, not physical-volume measures; Korean chip exports to China rose concurrently.
IEA September Hormuz flow 10.9 mb/d is not proof of 1 November deliveries; World Bank Brent figures are conditional annual forecasts.
